evidence: Single Django application with clear separation of concerns: core logic in 'treebeard/' package, tests in 'tests/', docs in 'docs/', and configuration in top-level files
Packages are organized by functional domain (e.g., tree implementations: mp_tree, ns_tree, al_tree, ltree) rather than technical layers
Low average fan-out (2.52) indicates limited cross-package dependencies, supporting modularity
No external service communication patterns (e.g., no REST/gRPC clients, message queues, or service discovery)
All components run in a single process with shared database and memory space
Django's built-in app structure (models, admin, forms, templatetags) used consistently within the treebeard package
Test suite is co-located with source code in a dedicated tests/ directory, typical of modular monoliths
Code maintainability metrics show moderate complexity (mi_avg ~70), consistent with a well-structured but non-trivial monolith
risks: Tight coupling between Django framework and core logic may reduce testability in isolation
Monolithic deployment could impact scalability and team autonomy as project grows
Shared database and process space increases risk of cascading failures
